data.narrative:
Corvus Robotics is a Series C-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jackie Wu and Mohammed Kabir. The valuation framework draws on a comparable universe of 9 private firms and 1 public company operating in the same sector and stage band, including Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the company's $28.2M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $48M. The peer-median approach examines 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. This dispersion reflects heterogeneous exit trajectories and capital efficiency within the cohort.

The triangulated analysis implies a broad range of $41M to $1.9B, with a median of $849M. The 46x spread between low and high reflects material method divergence: stage-progression anchors to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects achieved valuations in a well-capitalized segment. Key uncertainties include the company's revenue scale relative to peers, unit economics, and go-to-market traction—variables not present in this dataset. The peer set itself shows wide dispersion by stage (Series B through D), limiting precision. A credible mid-point estimate would require disclosure of revenue or ARR metrics and narrowing of the comparable stage band.
